mission: SINGLE CANARY #2B - fix only the structural ownership problem behind canary #2's 10 obvious false gaps. Do not put the connective words back into FUNCTION_WORDS. No other audit defect addressed.
primaryPositiveFixture: I5: "...not to exceed $40,000,000; provided that no Default has occurred and is continuing; provided further that, if the Total Leverage Ratio exceeds 4.00 to 1.00, such amount shall not exceed $20,000,000." with MATERIAL items on the permission, the condition and the alternative
negativeFixture: S9 (canary #2's safety control): "The Borrower shall not make any Investment, except as provided in Section 6.02, at any time prior to the Maturity Date." with MATERIAL items on the two outer clauses only
rootStructuralCause: Both fixtures have the IDENTICAL span shape - an UNACCOUNTED connective fragment immediately followed by a COVERED_BY_INVENTORY clause with only whitespace between - so adjacency, brevity and neighbouring coverage cannot separate them. What separates them is whether the fragment carries an object of its own. ", provided that" contributes nothing but the attachment of the clause that follows it; ", except as provided in Section 6.02," carries a cross-reference that IS the content of the exception, so no amount of coverage of the following clause accounts for it.

ownershipRule.disposition: COVERED_BY_CONNECTIVE_OWNERSHIP (new, auditable, in the ACCOUNTED set)
allConditionsRequired: the fragment has at least one content word and EVERY content word is a clause-introducing connective
the fragment carries no digit (a locator such as '6.02' is an object)
the fragment carries no reference noun (section/clause/paragraph/subsection/article/annex/exhibit/schedule/appendix)
the fragment carries no quoted term
the fragment carries no quantitative value
the very next span in the region is COVERED_BY_INVENTORY, with only whitespace between - so no independent clause and no clause terminator intervenes
that complement's coverage BEGINS where the connective ends, so the covered clause is the one the connective introduces
the complement is substantive in its own right (it has content words of its own)
ownershipRule.onUncertainty: UNACCOUNTED_SOURCE - the fragment stays a gap
ownershipRule.notKeyedTo: no rule mentions I5, S9, Section 6.02, any section number, any corpus id, or the specific words 'provided'/'except' as special cases; the connective set is a generic class and membership alone discharges nothing
ownershipRule.notwithstandingExcluded: 'notwithstanding' is deliberately NOT a clause-introducing connective. It is an OVERRIDE operator whose complement is the provision being disapplied, which lives elsewhere in the agreement; covering the text that follows it does not account for the override relationship. This is why I27 remains a review gap - by design, not by optimisation.
